section.title: Overview
section.para: The lost module is a client for the two HTTP-based protocols an Emergency-CSCF needs in order to route an emergency call:

listitem.para: HELD (HTTP Enabled Location Delivery, RFC 6155) to ask a Location Information Server (LIS) where the caller is, and to dereference a location URI (RFC 6753).
LoST (Location-to-Service Translation, RFC 5222) to ask an Emergency Call Routing Function (ECRF) which PSAP serves that location for a given service URN (RFC 5031).

section.para: The caller location is taken from the PIDF-LO carried by the request: either by value from a multipart/related body part referenced by a Geolocation: <cid:...> header (which is what a 3GPP UE sends, see TS 24.229), or by reference from a Geolocation: <https://...> header, or passed directly as a function parameter.
All HTTP work is delegated to the rest_client module, so TLS, connection reuse and timeouts behave exactly as they do there.

section.title: Asynchronous Operation
section.para: Every exported function is available both as a regular function and as an async one. Since an emergency call needs two serial round trips to external servers, running them synchronously blocks a SIP worker for the entire duration of the exchange. Prefer the async flavour:

example.title: Asynchronous location retrieval and mapping

section.para: Only the first HTTP exchange of a function call is asynchronous. Two secondary exchanges are always performed synchronously, because both are avoidable in practice:

listitem.para: the dereference of a locationURI when a HELD locationResponse contains no presence element — dereference the returned URI yourself with an async instead;
following a LoST redirect, which does not happen with the default setting, since the mapping server then resolves the chain itself.

section.title: Return Codes
section.para: All functions return a positive value on success and a negative one on failure, so they can be tested directly in a condition. The magnitude carries the detail and is available in $rc:

listitem.para: 200 — success. refines this to 201 when the response held a location reference, 202 a location value, and 203 both.
-400 — the exchange failed locally: bad parameters, no location found, transport error, or a non-2xx HTTP status.
-500 — the LIS or ECRF answered with a protocol error response. The error code or type is written to the err output variable.

section.para: Note that the output variables are only written when the exchange completed, so a script must check the return code before using them.

section.title: &osips; Modules
section.para:
The following modules must be loaded before this module:
rest_client — performs all HTTP transfers.
tls_mgm — only when a connection uses the tls_dom property.

section.title: External Libraries or Applications
section.para:
The following libraries or applications must be installed before running &osips; with this module loaded:
libxml2.

section.title: connection (string)
section.para: Defines a named LIS or ECRF server, which the exported functions then reference by name. The format is:

listitem.para: url (mandatory) — the HTTP(S) endpoint.
timeout — maximum duration of a transfer, in seconds. Defaults to the rest_client curl_timeout setting.
tls_dom — a tls_mgm client domain, for server verification and client certificates (mutual TLS).

section.para: The parameter may be set multiple times. Names must be unique.

section.title: location_type (string)
section.para: The locationType requested from the LIS. Any combination of civic, geodetic, locationURI and any, separated by spaces.

section.title: exact_type (integer)
section.para: When set to 1, the locationRequest asks for an exact match of (exact="true"), meaning the LIS must return every requested type or fail.

section.title: response_time (integer)
section.para: The responseTime of a locationRequest, in milliseconds. A value of 0 requests emergencyRouting, i.e. the fastest answer the LIS can give.

section.title: post_request (integer)
section.para: When set to 1, a location URI is dereferenced with a HELD locationRequest POST instead of a plain GET.

section.title: geoheader_type (integer)
section.para: Which kind of Geolocation header value to use:

listitem.para: 0 — any (first one found)
1 — cid: only, i.e. location by value from the message body
2 — HTTP(S) URI only, i.e. location by reference

section.title: geoheader_order (integer)
section.para: Which locationValue to use when the request carries more than one, whether in a single Geolocation header or spread over several (RFC 6442 §4.2.1): 0 for the first, 1 for the last.

section.title: geoheader_incl_alt (integer)
section.para: When set to 1, altitude is kept in the location sent to the mapping server. Most ECRFs only map latitude and longitude.

section.title: location_profile (integer)
section.para: A findService request carries exactly one location, so when the PIDF-LO holds several — a compound civic and geodetic location, as RFC 5491 §3.2 allows — this parameter picks which one is used. The others are dropped with a warning.

listitem.para: 0 — the first location, of any type
1 — the last location, of any type
2 — the first geodetic location
3 — the first civic location

section.para: With 2 or 3 the query fails when the PIDF-LO holds no location of that type, so 0 or 1 are the safer settings unless the mapping server only accepts one profile. RFC 5491 §3 rule 7 requires the coarser location to come first in a compound location, which is why 0 is the default.

section.title: recursion (integer)
section.para: Sets recursive="true" on a findService request, asking the mapping server to resolve any referral itself. With 0, the module follows redirects on its own, synchronously.

section.title: verbose (integer)
section.para: When set to 1, the parsed contents of every findServiceResponse are written to the log.

title.function: lost_query(con, uri, name, err[, pidf[, urn]])

section.para: Sends a LoST findService request to a mapping server and returns the URI of the serving PSAP.
Parameters:

listitem.para: con (string) — name of a . If no such connection exists, the value is treated as a domain and resolved via a LoST:https or LoST:http NAPTR lookup.
uri (var) — output: the PSAP URI.
name (var) — output: the PSAP display name.
err (var) — output: the LoST error type, if the mapping server returned an error response.
pidf (string, optional) — the PIDF-LO to map. When absent, it is taken from the Geolocation header, as controlled by .
urn (string, optional) — the service URN to map. Defaults to the Request URI.

section.para: See .
This function can be used from any route. An async variant is available.

section.para: Sends a HELD locationRequest to a LIS and returns the caller location.

pidf (var) — output: the returned PIDF-LO.
url (var) — output: the returned location URI, if the response carries a locationUriSet.
err (var) — output: the HELD error code, if the LIS returned an error response.
id (string, optional) — the device identity to ask about. Defaults to P-Asserted-Identity, then From.
